audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart rows 1-4 read "Skill" while the content layer and the packet chart both read "Mel" — the page renders two answers to who wins Level 1.
audit.why: Mel's Radiant Volley (Q, 950 range, 10s at rank 1) and Solar Snare (E, 1000 range root, 11s) both outrange Anivia's safe farming pattern before Glacial Storm, and Rebuttal (W) reflects Flash Frost. Anivia's 56.18% over 858 games comes after level 6, not before it.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side flipped to Mel so both layers agree; rows 5-7 stay Anivia.

audit.why: Spikes are correctly ordered: Lost Chapter mana spike, level 6 Glacial Storm inversion, first-item burst, late-game zone control. Mel's own spike is Golden Eclipse at 6 (120s rank 1) and its Overwhelm scaling per rank.
audit.corrected: Sharpened spikes[0] and spikes[2] to name the real ability and its real downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text invents a Mel ability called "Reflected Radiance" and calls Rebuttal a "sidestep tool". It also never states the decisive interaction: Rebuttal reflects Flash Frost back at Anivia, and Golden Eclipse is a global execute off stacked Overwhelm.
audit.why: Riot's text: Rebuttal "forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage". Flash Frost is flagged projectile. Rebuttal's cooldown is 38/35/33/29/26 — the longest window in her kit and the whole green light. Golden Eclipse has 25000 range and scales with Overwhelm stacks, so distance does not save you.
audit.corrected: Named Rebuttal and Solar Snare correctly, stated the reflect, and keyed poke timing to Rebuttal's 38s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Golden Eclipse is a threshold cash-out you cannot walk away from.
audit.why: Overwhelm stacks infinitely and R strikes every marked enemy regardless of distance; the missingInteractions entry flags exactly this.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Mel

edits.before: He needs a full combo to pop the egg AND the bird — make the combo cost a stun to attempt.
edits.after: She needs Solar Snare to land first — deny the root and Golden Eclipse never finds the egg.

edits.before: Make him kill you twice through a stun and a wall — then storm the wave he stopped farming. Shorthand: Rebuttal down, wave right, go.
edits.after: Make her kill you twice through a wall and a stun — then storm the wave she stopped farming. Shorthand: Rebuttal down, wave right, go.

edits.before: Mel wins by landing Rebuttal, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Mel wins by landing Solar Snare, stacking Overwhelm with Radiant Volley, then cashing it in with a global R.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Mel burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Poke Q only once Rebuttal is down — through it, your own Flash Frost comes back at you. Land Q, then E for the doubled chill damage and walk.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Mel walks straight at you.
edits.after: Throwing Q into a glowing Rebuttal — it returns to you, feeds her Overwhelm, and leaves no stun for the Solar Snare that follows.

edits.before: - Mel Rebuttal: matchup-defining — Reflects your projectiles back — never poke while it glows. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Crystallize has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Rebuttal: 38s at rank 1, 26s maxed — it reflects Flash Frost back at you, so every poke waits on it. - Solar Snare: 11s, her only setup; dodge it and the all-in dies. - Wall for the moment it goes wrong, R for when it goes right.

edits.before: If Mel opens the score, reset expectations and respect Rebuttal doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Mel opens the score, stop poking entirely — reflected Q is how the second death happens. Farm with R wave-clear, hold the wall for Solar Snare, and stay above the Overwhelm cash-out number.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by denying her the 1000-range angles: storm the choke so Radiant Volley has no safe ground, and wall the line Solar Snare wants to travel.

edits.before: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Mel away from the comeback farm, and rotate first to every river fight with your stun loaded.
edits.after: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Mel off the comeback farm, and step up only in the 26-38s her Rebuttal is down — she has no dash to leave with.

edits.before: Q only — last-hit with autos and save the stun strictly for his step-ups. Your egg is NOT a license to int level 1.
edits.after: Q only — last-hit with autos and hold the stun; into a raised Rebuttal it flies back at you. Your egg is NOT a license to int level 1.

edits.before: Q-E online — a landed stun now means a real chunk. Trade only when his engage tool is down; your mana hates wasted rotations.
edits.after: Q-E online — a landed stun now means a real chunk. Trade only with Rebuttal on its 38s cooldown; your mana hates reflected rotations.

edits.before: Reflects your projectiles back — never poke while it glows. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Rebuttal reflects Flash Frost back at you and blanks the damage — 38s at rank 1 is your whole green-light window.

edits.before: That is Mel’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse hits from anywhere and scales on stacked Overwhelm — watch the number, not the bar.

edits.before: Mel's Radiant Volley poke and Reflected Radiance shield let her out-trade your slow wind-up spells and punish any Flash Frost miss with free damage.
edits.after: Mel's Radiant Volley poke and Rebuttal (W) let her out-trade your slow wind-up spells — Rebuttal reflects Flash Frost straight back at you for free damage.

edits.before: Liandry's/Rylai's burst lets you punish her immobility the instant she's out of Reflected Radiance charges, closing the damage gap fast.
edits.after: Liandry's/Rylai's burst lets you punish her immobility inside the 26-38s Rebuttal is down, closing the gap before Overwhelm stacks cash out.

edits.before: Mel's poke and shield win the early trades before your kit comes online
edits.after: Radiant Volley and Rebuttal win the early trades before your kit lands

edits.before: Her shielded poke still holds the lane advantage into level 5
edits.after: Solar Snare into Radiant Volley still holds the lane into level 5

edits.before: Bait out her Reflected Radiance shield before committing Flash Frost
edits.after: Bait Rebuttal (W) out with an auto before committing Flash Frost

edits.before: Reflect your engage damage back with her shield passive
edits.after: Reflect your Flash Frost back at you with Rebuttal (W)

notes: Mel is female; the full layer referred to her as "he/his" in tldr, winCon and phases[0-1].why — fixed in the rewrites. "Reflected Radiance" is fabricated; the real ability is Rebuttal (W). Level chart rows 1-4 disagreed across layers (full said Skill, content said Mel); flipped the full side to Mel to match content and packet. Ratings on rows 0-3 left at 5/10 — flagged in questionsForUser whether they should drop with the side flip. Frostbite (E) is targeted, not flagged projectile, so I did not assert whether Rebuttal blocks it. | COHERENCE: 3 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
